  • Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.
  • Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that it’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s fresh financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a upcoming contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

United also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January.

Pochettino is only expected to make two fresh signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre).

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

According to recent reports, yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55.
  • Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.
  • On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55.

Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.

On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.

Not only are Villa now outsiders to finish in the top eight of the league phase, they have now gone six matches without a win in all competitions.

When quizzed on the prolonged wait for Garnacho to make his first Villa start, Emery has often been encouraging towards the Chelsea loanee.

However, when asked about his absence from the squad in Turkey, Emery hinted that the winger is not in his prepares.

Emery named 11 substitutes - with two goalkeepers - for the Galatasaray game, one fewer than he was permitted.

Questioned over Garnacho not being involved, he told reporters: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us.".

At his pre-match press conference, Emery stated that everyone was available, apart from Matty Cash, Matteo Ruggeri, Amadou Onana and the ineligible Brian Madjo.

Emery has been facing suggestions that Garnacho has been discarded from his aims in the same fashion as Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott in 2025-26 since September.

He seemingly spoke sincerely when saying that Garnacho had made a positive impact during training and a friendly during the September international break.

However, he remains with just 64 minutes across four substitute appearances since September 5. Although the appearances required for a permanent transfer from Chelsea has never been confirmed, the assumption is that it is 10 matches.

Garnacho is on seven outings, and there is now little to no realistic prospect of Emery choosing to activate a clause that would require Villa to pay approximately £43m for his signature.

As much as Villa's hierarchy and fans back Emery, questions need to be asked how two loanees who are known to have buy clauses in their respective agreements have been frozen out so quickly.

In a recent development, villa have agreed separate deals worth a combined total of £78m. Elliott and Garnacho have made just three starts - all for Elliott - between them.

Amorim proud of ‘intelligent, courageous’ Milan, world-class Rabiot and Ramos

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.
  • Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was notable that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team revealed the levels that they are capable of.

Industry observers note that now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it indicated towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

Recent findings suggest that “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

Recent findings suggest that “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

“I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

“The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

Industry observers note that “But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

“Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

It has been revealed that “Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an important objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

According to recent reports, “Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.

Breaking: Brest vs Paris FC - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 24 Nov 2026 23:33.
  • In a matchup featuring two of Ligue 1's biggest surprise stories at the moment, Brest will welcome Paris FC to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Friday.
  • A 1-0 win at Strasbourg on matchday 11 lifted the Brittany side to sixth in the Ligue 1 table, five points behind Paris, who are second after a convincing 4-0 triumph over Angers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 24 Nov 2026 23:33.

In a matchup featuring two of Ligue 1's biggest surprise stories at the moment, Brest will welcome Paris FC to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Friday.

A 1-0 win at Strasbourg on matchday 11 lifted the Brittany side to sixth in the Ligue 1 table, five points behind Paris, who are second after a convincing 4-0 triumph over Angers.

It appears as though Julien Lachuer has finally figured out the right buttons to push to help Brest find some consistency domestically.

This team entered November having dropped points in four of their last five league fixtures, but they will boast a 100% record this month should they triumph on Friday.

Brest can also win at least four domestic affairs in a row for the first time in a single league season since 2023-24 when they claimed six consecutive victories in this competition.

With a win on matchday 12, they would temporarily move into third place in Ligue 1 and that final Champions League spot above Lille on goal difference.

A team that gave up at least one goal in each of their first eight matches in this competition have not conceded in their last three such games.

After 11 matchdays, Les Pirates are third in Ligue 1 regarding expected goals but also rank third in massive chances missed (23).

Liam Rosenior must be happy to be back in France, managing in a league where he has found tremendous success as a head coach.

The man who guided Strasbourg to a place in the Conference League has transformed Paris FC into title contenders, with his side just three points below Paris Saint-Germain heading into this match.

A victory by three or more goals on Friday would temporarily put them in first place and extend their winning run in this competition to four matches.

Right now, Paris FC are averaging 2.09 points per match in this competition, which is 0.80 more than a season ago, the biggest such increase among Ligue 1 clubs over that span.

They boast the lowest expected goals conceded in the league (10.2) and are one of three teams in the top flight that have not allowed a set-piece goal so far, with PSG and Lens being the others.

Paris FC can earn a third successive Ligue 1 triumph versus Brest on Friday, beating them 2-1 in their last visit to Stade Francis-Le Ble a season ago.

A calf strain may keep Brendan Chardonnet out of the Brest fold on Friday, while Kenny Lala is questionable with a knock and Kamory Doumbia is also doubtful with an ankle injury.

Noah Edjouma netted his third of the competition last week, while Egil Selvik stopped five shots to collect his third successive clean sheet in Ligue 1.

Meanwhile, for Paris FC, Nhoa Sangui may miss another match because of a hamstring issue which he has struggled to recover from.

Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all found the back of the net on matchday 11, with each strike coming in the second half.

Brest possible starting lineup:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.
  • Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals.
  • ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

Sources indicate that at the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

According to recent reports, one expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he mentioned, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

According to recent reports, england kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that england lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All said, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and mentioned he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

But on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Industry observers note that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

In a recent development, we played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

Industry observers note that [Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

Recent findings suggest that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone showed he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

He’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

Recent findings suggest that you saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

It has been revealed that it started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it promptly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

Industry observers note that this is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

Shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

England played the Czech Republic a week ago, winning 2-0 in Prague by virtue of Anthony Gordon’s cute header and Kane’s clever shot through a defender’s legs but they huffed and puffed for ages against a team harshly reduced to 10 men until they blew the house down. They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 00:26, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 02:43.
  • Brentford are reportedly among three Premier League clubs interested in signing Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor.
  • The Bees splashed out around £41m to recruit midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens in the summer in a club-record transfer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 00:26, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 02:43.

Brentford are reportedly among three Premier League clubs interested in signing Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor.

The Bees splashed out around £41m to recruit midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens in the summer in a club-record transfer.

Sangare has featured in all 11 of Brentford's Premier League games, but he has not always been a guaranteed starter due to the competition from Vitaly Janelt and Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Mathias Jensen is also available to Brentford boss Keith Andrews, who at the moment has plenty of options at his disposal in central midfield.

However, Jensen is out of contract at the end of the season, and the uncertainty surrounding his future may be one of the factors behind Brentford's apparent interest in Taylor.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the Bees are one of three Premier League clubs that are keeping tabs on the Dutchman's performances at Lazio.

Bournemouth and Newcastle United are also showing a keen interest as they scour the market for potential midfield recruits.

The Cherries are believed to view Taylor as a potential replacement for Alex Scott, who continues to draw interest from some of the Premier League's biggest clubs.

Meanwhile, Newcastle appear to be still open to bolstering a midfield that lost the services of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali at the end of last season, despite recruiting Nico Gonzalez and Aladji Bamba in the summer window.

Taylor has played regularly since joining Lazio from Ajax in January, contributing five goals and five assists in 34 competitive appearances.

In fact, he has registered two goals and three assists in 12 league matches this term, helping Gennaro Gattuso's side establish a two-point lead at the top of Serie A.

With Taylor under contract until June 2030, there is a belief his potential suitors will have to offer around €40m (£33m) to have any hope of prising him away from Lazio.

However, a January departure seems unlikely at this stage, with Gattuso keen to keep one of his key players for the club's title battle.

Brentford, Bournemouth and Newcastle will also have to be wary of rival interest from Juventus, who view him as the 'ideal' midfield target.

Adrien Rabiot heaped praise on Goncalo Ramos for what he does for the team, but he also explained what AC Milan’s ‘problem’ is.

Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1. Gabriele Calvani’s own goal put the home side ahead, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netted to make it a rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is a third consecutive league victory after the wins over Inter and Genoa and it moves the Rossoneri on to 27 points, back inside the Champions League places. Up next: a trip to Athens to face Olympiacos on Thursday in the Europa League, and a chance to demonstrate consistency.

It has been revealed that after the full-time whistle, Rabiot spoke alongside Ramos to both Sky and DAZN, offering his thoughts on what was a very successful evening in front of all the fans at San Siro. His words are via MilanNews.

Are you starting to build a good identity?

Sources indicate that “Our problem is that we have to be focused for 90 minutes. We did well today, even though we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal. As I said, we’re growing as a team: the quality of our play, the team spirit, the sacrifice for 90 minutes, and everyone.

“Gonçalo is the first to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very crucial player for us, and we have a lot of games: I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit. But everyone’s attitude was great today, and we have to keep it up.

Industry observers note that “In these last few games, when we play like this, when we’re so focused and manage to do what we work towards in training, I think we’re all enjoying ourselves, even tonight. We created a lot, we scored a lot of goals. What we have to focus on is enjoying playing together.”.

Why didn’t you shoot before the first goal?

According to recent reports, “I wanted Pulisic to score, but the defender came back quickly. It’s true that I could have shot, but I get more pleasure from providing an assist than from scoring. But I did the assist afterwards.”.

Industry observers note that “He does a great job. Not everyone understands it, but he does an incredible job. When we get in and score, it’s also credit to us. Then we feel happy when he scores, also because it gives him confidence. Good for us and for him, for everyone.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 25 Nov 2026 01:26.
  • Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.
  • The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 25 Nov 2026 01:26.

Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.

Doncaster Rovers head back into action on Thursday aiming to move clear of the relegation zone at the beginning of the League One weekend, having endured a difficult start to the campaign.

In their second season back in the third tier after promotion from League Two and a 14th-placed finish last time around, the Yorkshire outfit presently find themselves 20th having managed just 13 points from their first 14 outings, losing seven and winning just three of those.

Indeed, their last six outings have produced just four points, as Grant McCann's side broke up four defeats with a 2-0 home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, before falling to Luton Town and MK Dons away from home and experiencing mixed fortunes in a pair of cup ties against Rochdale and Kidderminster Harriers, losing to the latter in the FA Cup first round.

A trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City followed on Saturday, and the Rovers were at least able to bounce back from consecutive league defeats, twice falling behind and levelling through Jordan Thomas in the 78th minute and Sean Grehan deep into injury time to leave with a creditable point from a 2-2 draw.

Still only leading the bottom four on goal difference, Doncaster Rovers will now aim to bounce back to winning ways to put themselves three points above the drop zone before the rest of the weekend's action.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors arrive in search of a rebound of their own to return to the top of the table.

Beginning their third straight season in League One and their first full one under the management of Martin Drury with the hopes of battling for promotion back to the second tier, Huddersfield Town have enjoyed a strong start as they headed into the November international break in top spot on 29 points from 14 games.

The Terriers won eight and only lost one of those while scoring 28 goals and conceding just 12, having headed into that break in a seven-game league unbeaten run in which they won four in a row before drawing against fellow promotion-chasers Luton Town in early November.

Then following a brief international break and a pair of cup outings against Exeter City and Liverpool Under-21s, Drury's side returned at home to Leicester City on Saturday but fell to just a second loss of the season in the third tier as Louis Page scored the only goal of the game for the visitors early in the second half.

That saw Huddersfield Town fall three points behind fresh leaders Stockport County, albeit with a game in hand, but only ahead of third-placed Oxford United having played a game more, and they will hope to quickly put things right and retake their place at the summit with a Yorkshire derby win on Thursday.

Huddersfield Town League One form:.

Doncaster Rovers remain without James Husband, Tommi O'Reilly and Francis Okoronkwo due to ongoing injuries, while Harry Clifton and Will Keane missed the game against Bradford and will likely remain sidelined too.

Brandon Hanlan led the line in that game and may continue to do so with Alfie May ineligible against his parent club, although James Collins is back in contention having made his Rovers league debut off the bench at the weekend following a long layoff.

Elsewhere, George Broadbent should again join Robbie Gotts and mainstay Owen Bailey in midfield.

Huddersfield Town are still without Murray Wallace, Jack Whatmough, David Kasumu, Herbie Kane and Marcus McGuane through injuries.

Drury should avoid making many changes despite the weekend's defeat, with Radinio Balker, Ibane Bowat and Sean Roughan having formed a strong back three in recent weeks and Cameron Humphreys and Archie Collins likely to continue their midfield partnership.

Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes have shone in attack, with the former scoring 10 goals in 14 league games and the latter notching up seven goals and six assists in 15.

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Simkin; Nixon, Grehan, Pearson, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Hutchinson, Bailey, Thomas; Hanlan.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:.

Young; Bowat, Balker, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Collins, Humphreys, Mumba; Sanches Fernandes, Taylor, Radulovic.

Huddersfield Town will hope their rare defeat at the weekend does not derail their promotion push, and despite the hosts taking a point from Bradford at the weekend, we back the Terriers to bounce back on Thursday and outclass Doncaster.

Latest Update: The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.
  • Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian remarked, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England.

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

In a recent development, what the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed fresh 100,000 stadium.

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed new 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

Recent findings suggest that it cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

Recent findings suggest that united travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Recent findings suggest that andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

In a recent development, fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

It has been revealed that diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

In a recent development, forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Recent findings suggest that juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La Liga side, Sevilla, have reportedly set their sights on a January transfer move for Birmingham City winger, Carlos Vicente, less than a year on from the Spaniard's initial move to St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

That is according to Vamos Mi Sevilla, with the Spanish giants at the moment sixth in their top-flight, having taken 19 points from 13 matches.

Birmingham endured a mixed 2025/26 Championship campaign, but have shown signs that they can potentially mount a sustained promotion bid this term, with Wednesday night's 2-0 success over Burnley seeing them remain fourth.

Vicente was one of two high-profile signings made by the Second City outfit in January, with his move from Deportivo Alaves coming days after seven-goal forward, August Priske, was recruited from Djurgardens IF.

It hasn't been the smoothest of rides for the 27-year-old at St. Andrew's, and he could be on the move once again if his former boss, Luis Garcia Plaza, sees his transfer wish granted.

Vicente was heavily courted by Blues having shone for Deportivo Alaves under Plaza's management, scoring 17 times and posting 13 assists in 82 appearances for his former club.

Such was their desire to retain the winger's services, it was suggested the Championship side needed to pay £17.3m for his signature, before the initial fee was whittled down to £7m as Vicente penned a three-and-a-half year contract in the West Midlands.

Davies has since utilised the wide man's services on 36 occasions, with Vicente scoring five times and posting two assists, but it has emerged that Plaza is wishing to reunite with his former star at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan Stadium.

Reports state that Vicente also has a desire to return to his home country, and that Sevilla are exploring the possibility of an initial loan swoop, which could be made permanent in the summer, by which time the winger will have 24 months' left on his Birmingham contract.

Vicente made 17 Championship appearances in the second half of last season, with his best form coming in the final weeks of the campaign.

In a run of six successive starts to round off the season, the Spaniard netted his first goals against Ipswich Town and Wrexham, and continued to keep Patrick Roberts out of the starting lineup in the current campaign's early weeks.

Despite goals, again, in back-to-back outings against Norwich City and Derby County in September, a strong run of form from Roberts saw Vicente dropped to the bench, before he made a strong impact in his first start in a month in the victory against Burnley in midweek.

During the encounter, the winger created three chances and set Jay Stansfield free for the club-record signing to provide Priske with his seventh-minute opener.

It remains to be seen what Vicente's immediate future holds considering his impact from the get-go against the Clarets, as well as the sheer number of fixtures Birmingham have to contest in the coming weeks.

What does make such exit discourse particularly interesting, though, is that it has coincided with reports suggesting that Blues are, again, plotting a move for Liel Abada, formerly of Celtic, alongside local and promotion rivals, Wolves.

Blues fans, how do you assess Carlos Vicente's situation at St. Andrew's? Comment below!

Abada is capable of featuring on both flanks, whilst Davies certainly isn't short of options at present through the likes of Vicente, Roberts, Demarai Gray and Liam Millar.

As such, this is an intriguing predicament, especially with the January window notoriously hard for conducting vast amounts of business.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
  • Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

Recent findings suggest that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

Recent findings suggest that the Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Sources indicate that dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

According to recent reports, the defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical proposal was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the complications exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

According to recent reports, pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

For Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 01:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 01:51.

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has brushed off Ballon d'Or talk after inspiring his side to a commanding 5-1 Champions League comeback victory over PSV Eindhoven.

The 23-year-old England international started Tuesday's league phase encounter at the Santiago Bernabeu on the bench as Jose Mourinho opted to manage his workload following recent fatigue.

With Los Blancos trailing 1-0 at the interval to an Ivan Perisic penalty, Mourinho summoned Bellingham at half-time and the substitute immediately transformed the contest.

After Federico Valverde restored parity five minutes into the second period, Bellingham put the hosts ahead on the hour mark with a sensational strike before later setting up Vinicius Junior's late fifth.

Bellingham's decisive go-ahead strike immediately drew comparisons to club icon Zinedine Zidane, whose famous number five shirt the Englishman wears in the Spanish capital.

Collecting the ball on the edge of the penalty area, the midfielder flicked it up with his first touch before slicing an audacious outside-of-the-boot volley inside the far post.

Speaking after the final whistle, Bellingham admitted the acrobatic effort stood above anything else he has produced in his career so far.

"I think this was the best goal of my life," Bellingham said, as reported by Fabrizio Romano.

@FabrizioRomano That was a prefect goal https://t.co/4j8kLOdUMX.

Teammate Bernardo Silva echoed the widespread awe inside the stadium, describing the strike as "one of those moments when you just go, 'Wow!'".

Bellingham's dazzling second-half appearance prompted Mourinho to reiterate his belief that omitting the midfielder from the top 10 at this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony was jarring.

The Portuguese tactician also conceded that leaving his talisman out of the starting lineup had backfired, admitting he had mistakenly believed Madrid could win without him.

When pressed on the prestigious individual accolade afterwards, however, Bellingham made it clear that collective silverware remains his sole obsession.

"Ballon d'Or? I do not care," he declared. "It's for journalists, not for me. I want to win all titles with Real Madrid.".

Having helped Los Blancos preserve their 100% start in the Champions League league phase, Bellingham will now look to carry his sparkling form back into La Liga action this weekend.

Mourinho's team are three points off Barcelona in the La Liga table ahead of their next match against Alaves.

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane has criticised the players’ performance and questioned supporters applauding them after Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, insisting the early red card was no excuse for the manner of the loss.

Industry observers note that mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge unravelled when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes at Anfield. Liverpool scored twice inside 13 minutes and added two more goals after the break, leaving United 19th in the Premier League.

Speaking on Sky Sports, Keane challenged the suggestion that United’s performance was understandable because they had played most of the match with 10 men.

In a recent development, “Fans are applauding. Applauding what?” he asked, before describing the performance as “rubbish”.

Keane argued that United should have shown greater fight and quality, claiming Liverpool could have scored eight or nine goals. He also questioned why responsibility for the club’s problems so often fell on managers, owners and executives rather than the players themselves.

It has been revealed that some travelling supporters applauded the team after the final whistle, potentially recognising the difficulty of playing more than 80 minutes with a numerical disadvantage. Keane, however, viewed the reaction as evidence of declining expectations.

Sources indicate that keane also challenged fellow former United captain Gary Neville, who had suggested the early dismissal made the result more understandable. Neville was far from satisfied with United’s performance, though, and separately accused the club’s hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen the defence.

The disagreement reflected two concerns surrounding United: the players’ response to adversity and the quality of the squad available to Pochettino. Liverpool’s goals came from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the hosts creating numerous further opportunities.

Pochettino defended his players’ commitment afterwards and questioned Yoro’s dismissal, arguing that Alexander Isak had not established control of the ball when the defender challenged him. United have taken just eight points from 11 Premier League matches, leaving their fresh manager with little time to improve results. They travel to Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action.

Keane’s criticism adds to the scrutiny surrounding the squad following another heavy defeat to their fiercest rivals. For Pochettino, the immediate challenge is to improve defensive organisation while restoring confidence in a side struggling near the bottom of the table.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament upgrade confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

Industry observers note that for supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

According to recent reports, the concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Enzo brings a different tension.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring problem ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to blueprint around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Sources indicate that enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

Stoke continue their incredible run of form in the Championship, making it 11 wins, two draws, and one defeat in their 14 league games, after having lost all three of their opening games.

The Potters have emerged as surprise automatic promotion contenders this season, and with West Ham United away on Saturday, face arguably their biggest task yet since this mighty run of form began.

Back-to-back home victories over Birmingham City and Millwall mean they will head to the capital full of confidence, as the goalscorer from those games has drawn attention on social media.

George Hirst joined Stoke in the summer window from Ipswich Town for an initial £6 million, rising to £10 million, and with just one goal in his first 14 Championship games for the club, drew criticism from some supporters.

However, after netting the only goal in Stoke's 1-0 victory over Birmingham and both of the Potters' goals in their 2-1 win over Millwall, the Scottish international has silenced a few doubters, with his goal celebration against Blues not going unnoticed.

According to recent reports, celebrating his goal against Birmingham with Luke Graham, Hirst mimed spreading butter on bread, a nod to his interview whilst with Ipswich, where he scored a late penalty, incidentally against Blues, saying in his post-match interview: "[Scoring the penalty] is what I'm paid to do. It is my bread and butter.".

Now, some Stoke players have seemingly picked up on this, and taken to Instagram to react to his recent brace against Millwall.

Setting up Hirst's first goal against the Lions was American international Jack McGlynn, who has adapted tremendously to English football following his late summer switch from Houston Dynamo.

The midfielder has been a revelation for the Potters, and among their most important players this season, and alongside star shot-stopper Viktor Johansson, has taken to social media to react to Hirst's brace.

With just two simple bread and butter emojis, McGlynn and Johansson know exactly what they're making a nod to, and if Hirst continues to score at the rate he has over the past couple of games, it certainly won't be the last time those pair use those emojis this season.

What do you make of McGlynn and Johansson's nod to Hirst's celebration? Do you think Stoke can continue this run of form? Share your thoughts below!

With Hirst undergoing a slow start to life upon his move to Stoke, he has certainly silenced some of his doubters this week.

Lamine Cisse's injury has afforded the Scot a run of games in the side, though with both Sam Gallagher and Robert Bozenik waiting in the wings, Hirst must ensure he keeps firing at this rate if he wants to keep his place in the side.

There is growing optimism around the Potteries right now that this year could be Stoke's year, and Mark Robins will be hoping Hirst can keep firing them in at this rate to ensure that dream becomes a reality.

Manchester United have notified the Football Association of their intention to appeal against Leny Yoro’s red card during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, with captain Bruno Fernandes among those questioning the decision.

In a recent development, the French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak outside the penalty area. Referee Sam Barrott ruled that Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the resulting free-kick.

Mauricio Pochettino questioned whether Isak would have reached the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, a view shared by midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”.

It has been revealed that “To make a mistake like this can change a game,” he mentioned, as reported by the Press Association. The Portuguese midfielder nevertheless accepted that United were responsible for conceding from the subsequent free-kick.

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher offered a different assessment on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch programme, supporting Barrott’s decision while acknowledging the uncertainty over whether Isak would have reached the ball before Lammens.

“I think most people would have expected a red card,” Gallagher said.

An attacker’s likelihood of retaining or regaining possession is among the factors referees must consider when assessing whether a foul has denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United host Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday in Pochettino’s first home match in charge. Unless the appeal succeeds, Yoro will serve a one-match suspension against the Bees. United sit 19th in the Premier League, having won just one of their opening 11 matches. Yoro remains eligible for Wednesday’s Champions League fixture against Sporting, before attention turns to a crucial domestic fixture for Pochettino’s side.

Industry observers note that they’ve overachieved so far, but now they might need to be a bit more prudent. And what about Milan? If they don’t turn their trip to Athens into a Greek tragedy, perhaps their European campaign can get back on track, too.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been identified as a potential target. The United States international worked under Pochettino at international level and has expressed a desire to leave the French club.

Writing in The Independent, Miguel Delaney suggests United could have scope to spend £150m in January, although such expenditure would affect the club’s longer-term recruitment intends. That figure does not represent a confirmed transfer budget, and United have yet to announce any agreement to sign a upcoming striker.

Pochettino’s immediate challenge is finding a solution with his existing squad. United face Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday before returning to domestic action against Brentford.

With more than a month before the transfer window opens, the Argentine has little choice but to find a way of improving United’s attacking output with the players already at his disposal.

Blackburn Rovers have officially confirmed that their side will be backed by a sell-out travelling contingent for the upcoming Lancashire derby against Bolton Wanderers at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

It has been a campaign of mixed fortunes for Rovers, with the side who many tipped for relegation at the beginning of the campaign at the moment 12th.

A 1-0 victory against Watford at Vicarage Road on Wednesday night saw Blackburn reach 25 points after 17 games, just three points outside the play-offs.

Such feats come after the news that Tony Mowbray would be stepping back from his role due to health reasons, with Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds right now overseeing matters on the touchline.

And it's fair to say the interim duo will not be short of backing against Steven Schumacher's side on Saturday week.

As the crow flies, there are just 10 miles which separate Ewood Park and the Toughsheet Community Stadium, with this region of the country known for several historic rivalries.

Rovers fans, of course, will not quite have the same feelings of animosity towards the Whites as they displayed against Burnley on November 22nd, but it is one of three eye-catching fixtures from their perspective - the other being against Preston North End.

Bolton, of course, returned to the Championship for the first time in seven years in May, renewing this particular Lancashire rivalry in the process.

Yet, whilst attendances at Ewood, largely due to Blackburn's ownership situation, remain heavily criticised, not many will do the same after Rovers confirmed that over 5,000 supporters will make the short journey for next weekend's early kick-off.

It was confirmed on November 20th that away supporters wanting to purchase a ticket for Blackburn's clash with Bolton could do so on a general sale basis, after those with 4,500 or more points on the club's loyalty scheme were given a two-day headstart.

Even if the journey is straightforward, those in the away end still had to part with a sizeable sum of cash, particularly if they are an adult-paying supporter.

Indeed, tickets in such brackets cost £36, whilst an adult wanting to take one junior supporter with them to the match still had to part with a combined £45 for the two tickets.

However, the aforementioned bundle was only available in the upper tier of the Toughsheet Community Stadium's away allocation.

This may come as little surprise too, as Bolton rank sixth in the Championship when it comes to the average price of a ticket for visiting supporters.

Given their recent four-point haul, Rovers now sit level with five other Championship sides in this particular metric, having taken 10 points from a possible 27 on the road.

Bolton, meanwhile, have failed to make their home ground the fortress it needs to be in order to consolidate, winning just two of their first nine matches at the Toughsheet.

Blackburn will look to pile on the misery in that regard, especially with the recent form displayed by Andri Gudjohnsen, whose father, Eidur, enjoyed two spells with the Whites.

Recent findings suggest that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

In a recent development, it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:12.

Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

While funding a deal for the 29-year-old Uruguay international would normally prove difficult, the potential sale of highly rated youngster Milton Delgado could hand Boca the financial firepower required.

Aston Villa are among a host of English clubs tracking the 21-year-old defensive midfielder, meaning a winter raid from Unai Emery's side could directly threaten Tottenham's midfield depth.

According to Argentine outlets El Crack Deportivo and El Intransigente via Sport Witness, Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme has already started preliminary work on re-signing Bentancur.

Riquelme views the Spurs stalwart as his preferred candidate to replace Delgado should the academy graduate depart La Bombonera in the coming months.

Bentancur progressed through Boca's youth ranks before earning a switch to Juventus in 2017 and is seen as the ideal experienced presence to anchor their upcoming continental campaign.

The South American outfit plan to reinvest the proceeds from Delgado's prospective transfer straight into a formal approach for their former player.

Delgado's stock has risen even further after he played the full 90 minutes in Boca's 2-0 Copa Sudamericana final triumph over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday.

Villa are reportedly preparing a formal January offer for Delgado after scouting the 21-year-old extensively across the past six months.

However, Emery's side are far from alone in the race, with Chelsea, Bournemouth, Brighton and West Ham United all linked with the youngster.

Boca are believed to have previously rejected a £7.5m bid from MLS side Atlanta United back in August, around the same time Chelsea and Bournemouth lodged initial enquiries for the young midfielder, who is valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

Portuguese outfit Porto are also believed to be monitoring developments from Europe, leaving Riquelme in a strong position to command a substantial fee if a bidding war erupts.

Even if Boca secure the necessary funds, convincing Bentancur to leave North London could prove complicated given that he signed a new long-term contract with Tottenham in October 2025 and has spent almost a decade competing at the top level in Europe.
