According to recent reports, the point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

It has been revealed that chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

Industry observers note that the German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Sources indicate that olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

The World Cup has sharpened the comparison.

Chelsea’s official France preview noted that Malo Gusto was in the same squad as N’Golo Kante and former Blues academy player Olise. It was a neat reminder of how many Chelsea strands sit inside Didier Deschamps’ group.

In a recent development, bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

That matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

In a recent development, olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

Sources indicate that this is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any fresh wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

It has been revealed that he is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

Chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has confirmed he spoke to Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg in private ahead of the two clubs meeting for the first time since Spygate on Friday night.

As all football fans will remember from a story that dominated English football at the time, Saints were expelled from the play-offs after they admitted sending an employee to watch Boro train ahead of their play-off semi-final.

Therefore, despite losing to the south coast outfit over two legs, it was Middlesbrough who went to Wembley, although they did lose the final to Hull.

The punishment didn’t end there for Southampton, who admitted spying on several other Championship rivals earlier in the season, and they started the current campaign with a four-point deduction.

Sources indicate that given everything that had gone on, the first meeting between the two clubs was always going to be a spicy affair, and they face each other at St. Mary’s Stadium on Friday night, in a game that has been chosen for live TV coverage.

With Hellberg previously calling Southampton’s actions ‘disgraceful’, as well as stating what went on ‘breaks my heart’, the talking points ahead of the game were always going to extend beyond what happens on the pitch.

And, when asked about his relationship with Hellberg, Saints chief Eckert tried to play things down, as he revealed to journalist Alfie House that the pair did have discussions before the season started.

“We've had a conversation on the phone and we saw each other at the EFL day before the season. We are two managers who will try to win a game and that's it.”.

You can understand Eckert’s comments here, and there’s no doubt that Hellberg will echo those words, as it’s all about trying to win the game.

Given everything that had gone on, the first time the two clubs met was always going to be a big deal though, and all eyes will be on the dugouts to see how the managers greet each other before kick-off.

But, both clubs are trying to move on from what happened, and, in some ways, they will just be glad to get this game out of the way, as a lot of the build-up and noise around the fixture is all based on last season.

Clearly, Middlesbrough were furious at what happened, but Saints will feel they were hit with a severe punishment, with the points deduction meaning they go into the game seven points behind Hellberg’s side, as opposed to three.

Ultimately, this is a huge game in the promotion race, and both clubs will know that they will be sending out a statement if they can emerge victorious.

Southampton have an exceptional home record this season, so they will fancy their chances, but a loss will leave a significant gap to Boro in the battle for a top two finish.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough know that Saints can apply real pressure to them with a win, and they risk dropping from first to fifth with a defeat on the south coast if results go against them this weekend.

What are your predictions for Southampton vs Middlesbrough? Let us know in the comments below.

So, there’s so much riding on this game in terms of the table, and that’s before you consider what a win could do for either side in helping them build momentum and to add to their confidence.

Obviously, Spygate just adds to it all, but this is a game that will have massive implications on the promotion race - which Eckert and Hellberg will be well aware of.

Published: 14:08 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:56 EST, 23 November 2026.

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

Industry observers note that the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'.

Recent findings suggest that pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'.

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training.

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time.

Everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

Recent findings suggest that asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

Industry observers note that 'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'.

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

In a recent development, 'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart emoji)'.

What position do you prefer to play?

In a recent development, “I definitely always try to contribute in all positions, and I definitely prefer to play in my own position, but I’m always available in all roles. Which position? I won’t say (laughs).”.

Where can you still grow and what does Amorim ask of you?

“I have to improve in many other areas. As always, scoring is always great. I’d also like to add a few assists for some of my team-mates, but the most vital thing was always to bring home three points, and today we did that.”.

Is there a team-mate you have to thank in particular?

How far along are you in your development?

Recent findings suggest that “Right now, I’m not even halfway there. Maybe even lower. There’s still a lot of work to do to get there. But I’m in the right place, and hopefully we can get there.”.

How much is Amorim protecting you?

“Progress is the right word, because we’ve changed coaches, and it’s never easy. We’re a great team, with many champions. We still have a lot of work to do. Milan always has our backs, and that’s very key to me.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

In a recent development, according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Sources indicate that manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

Industry observers note that “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

Recent findings suggest that that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

According to recent reports, within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

In a recent development, prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a massive boost. It could help fund new signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

According to recent reports, city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

It has been revealed that chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Serie A duo Como and Napoli are reportedly monitoring Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee ahead of the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old Netherlands international has struggled to secure regular playing time under multiple managers since arriving at Old Trafford from Bologna in the summer of 2024.

Zirkzee is yet to make a single Premier League start during the 2026-27 campaign, with all seven of his top-flight outings coming from the substitutes' bench.

After nearly leaving England on Deadline Day, when United rejected an approach from Everton, the attacker could now be set for a winter return to Italian football.

The forward has been earmarked as a possible early departure from Old Trafford under Mauricio Pochettino in January.

According to Sky Sports News, both Italian clubs are exploring a mid-season move but are waiting for clarity on Zirkzee's role under fresh United head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino was only appointed last week and handed the Dutchman a 45-minute second-half cameo during Sunday's chastening 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool.

No formal negotiations have been opened with the Red Devils hierarchy yet as suitors wait to discover whether the Argentine tactician considers the forward surplus to requirements.

Zirkzee has managed two goals across his limited substitute appearances this season, netting against Aston Villa in the league and ironically finding the back of the net against Como in the Champions League last month.

The Dutchman's previous pedigree in Italy, where he earned a spot in the Serie A Team of the Year with Bologna, ensures his stock remains high across the peninsula despite his Old Trafford struggles.

Both interested sides have urgent attacking voids to fill when the winter market opens for business.

Como boss Cesc Fabregas recently confirmed that striker Moise Kean faces several months on the sidelines after aggravating a recurring tibia concern in training.

Meanwhile, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri is seeking fresh firepower after Lorenzo Lucca struggled to make an impact following his return from a loan spell at Nottingham Forest.

With United already heavily linked with prolific strikers like Vangelis Pavlidis and Ivan Toney to spearhead Pochettino's rebuild, a January exit could ultimately suit all parties involved.

In a recent development, the Trotters have had an okay start to life back in the Championship after a seven-year absence. Last season's League One play-off winners' main goal would have been to stay in the division, and thus far, they've remained above the dotted line.

"I have spoken to Fergal and Owen, and we are very clear about areas of the team that we would like to strengthen," he continued.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

Sources indicate that however, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

“The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino remarked.

Industry observers note that “Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

In a recent development, “But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

In a recent development, the FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The duo led the Imps into their first Championship season since 1961 following Michael Skubala's summer exit to divisional rivals, Bristol City.
  • Lincoln coasted to last season's League One title, accumulating a staggering 103 points whilst also embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a third managerial figure this calendar year following the midweek decision to part ways with joint-managers, Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The duo led the Imps into their first Championship season since 1961 following Michael Skubala's summer exit to divisional rivals, Bristol City.

Lincoln coasted to last season's League One title, accumulating a staggering 103 points whilst also embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.

But as the final month of 2026 nears, they are the lowest-placed out of the three sides who earned promotion last term, having taken just 15 points from their first 17 matches.

It remains to be seen which direction is taken by owner, Ron Fowler at the ProAmpac Stadium, but it has emerged that a previous target, now working with another Championship club, has entered the managerial frame.

Lincoln are right now outside the relegation zone by three points, with Tuesday's heavy 4-0 defeat to Charlton Athletic at The Valley, coupled with the manner of their side's performance, spelt the end for Cohen and Shaw.

The Imps have won just one of their last six Championship matches, with it now emerging through Alan Nixon - via Patreon - that Gavin Strachan has been listed as a potential candidate.

Strachan, 47, is currently on the coaching staff at West Bromwich Albion under James Morrison, with the Baggies currently within three points of the Championship summit after a 3-1 win at Bolton Wanderers.

Prior to the start of the fresh season, the Aberdeen-born man spent six years at Celtic working under the likes of Brendan Rodgers, Ange Postecoglou and Martin O'Neill, with the Hoops winning the last five Scottish Premiership titles on offer.

Following on from Postecoglou's exit to Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, the Australian wished to take Strachan with him to North London, but a deal could not be agreed.

The aforementioned Morrison was appointed as permanent head coach of West Brom this summer after ensuring the Black Country side's survival in difficult circumstances.

As well as retaining Matt Gill, who had been linked with a switch to Leicester City, the former Scotland international midfielder opted to install Strachan and Tony McMahon as part of a fresh-look coaching setup.

Given how highly Strachan is rated on the coaching circuit, Morrison's initial words following the decision read: "I’m also delighted to add Gavin Strachan to the group.

"Having a fresh pair of eyes from somebody with Gavin’s experience will help us massively. He has worked alongside some top managers, like Martin O’Neill, Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers, and will no doubt bring fresh ideas with him.".

Prior to his spell with Celtic, Strachan also assisted Darren Ferguson in two spells at Peterborough United, as well as his stint with Doncaster Rovers.

The decision for the Imps to remove Cohen and Shaw from their positions as joint-managers was the sixth managerial change already made in this season's Championship.

Four of those have been made by clubs in a similar region of the table to Lincoln, with Watford, Burnley and Preston North End all replacing Alessio Dionisi, Nicky Hayen and Paul Heckingbottom with Edward Iordanescu, Fabio Celestini and Graham Alexander respectively.

Lincoln fans, would Gavin Strachan be a wise appointment at this particular moment? Comment below!

With the Reds needing to rediscover form, particularly on home turf, in a bid to survive against the odds, supporters will be hoping that the board get their next decision right.

However, it has already been confirmed that no final call will be made ahead of Saturday's daunting task of taking on Wolves, with Shaun Pearson taking interim charge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roma have put an £86m (€100m) price tag on Manu Koné, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, reviving the Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link that first emerged over the summer. Roma want any interested club, including Chelsea, to know the price before serious talks can even begin.

Koné remains under contract at the Stadio Olimpico, and he has become a key part of Roma’s midfield since his move from Borussia Mönchengladbach. The Gazzetta report reads like a warning to potential buyers rather than proof of any talks between the two clubs.

Roma sporting director Tony D’Amico has confirmed Chelsea made contact late in the summer window, though he was quick to draw a clear line under how far things went.

Industry observers note that “There was an inquiry and some preliminary contact with Chelsea on the final day of the transfer window. No official offers arrived that would allow us to approach the player. Something was imagined that simply didn’t happen. There was no official offer; the final day of the transfer window got everyone a little worked up.”.

In a recent development, D’Amico’s comments confirm Chelsea looked at signing Koné before the deadline, but they stop well short of showing an official bid was ever made. He also explained why Roma had no wish to sell a key player so close to the window closing.

“Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I said it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of vital players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

According to recent reports, koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

In a recent development, for now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

Nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. Paul Merson believes Manchester United must strengthen their defence in January but insists their problems extend beyond the backline, with concerns over their midfield and attacking options also needing attention.

According to recent reports, “Back in the day when it’s Rooney and them kind of players and Van Nistelrooy and Keane and Scholes and Beckham and Ronaldo, they were seven, eight out of ten every week. There wasn’t a four out of ten and a nine out of ten.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first South Wales derby between Swansea City and Cardiff City for just short of two years takes place on Sunday, and clarity has been provided regarding the hosts' search for a new head coach.

Swansea started the Championship campaign in fine fettle, leading the division as recently as October 17th under Vitor Matos, who then made the decision to join RC Strasbourg, much to the bemusement of those in South Wales.

The Portuguese was only installed as Alan Sheehan's replacement 12 months ago, winning 22 of his 47 matches in charge, with the last of those being the late loss at Birmingham City on November 7th.

Within a rather frosty announcement by the Welsh side, it was confirmed that Kris O'Leary, Ashley Williams, Joe Allen and Leon Britton were to lead the 2-2 draw against West Bromwich Albion last weekend, before also overseeing Tuesday's 2-1 loss to league leaders, Middlesbrough.

With ownership duo, Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen, seeking a swift replacement, clarity has now been provided as to who will lead the Swans for the weekend's grudge match against the Bluebirds.

Despite a recent dip in form, Swansea are narrowly outside the early-season play-off places, and, if results fall their way in the next 72 hours, they could return to the top eight.

The club's current situation has led to intense speculation over who could take the reins, with Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick initially linked, before reports emerged over the potential hire of Rosenborg boss, Freyr Alexandersson.

Alexandersson's current employers are currently fourth in the Norwegian Eliteserien and have three matches to play in a bid to secure European qualification.

Despite the 44-year-old acknowledging such links, it has been revealed by Sky Sports' Anthony Joseph that the quartet of Williams, O'Leary, Britton and Allen will take charge against Cardiff, and, potentially, the three subsequent fixtures as Alexandersson may see out the remainder of the campaign at the Lerkendal Stadion.

Unsurprisingly, the fact Swansea may now have to wait at least two more weeks for full clarity on who takes the long-term reins in the dugout has sparked an immediate reaction.

According to recent reports, one of many responses read: "Whilst the derby was always going to be a bit of a push. We can't wait until 13th, that's another 4 games and a significant amount of points on the table and then to ask him to settle over christmas period. It has to be now or never for me.".

Another wrote: "If we have to wait until 13th December, move on.".

"Will be like when we persisted with Sheehan last season, need a fresh manager in asap," noted another Swans fan.

"Potentially another 4 games in charge before we hire a latest manager is bonkers," backed up the general feeling amongst the fanbase.

It has been revealed that another fan gave an in-depth stance on the matter, replying: "Waiting until mid-December to make an appointment is potentially catastrophic for our season, especially when waiting for a manager with a completely unproven track record. December is the busiest stretch of the season, it’s not a month that you can afford to throw away.".

Swans fans, how are you feeling about this update ahead of the South Wales derby? Comment below!

In a recent development, however, some took a more philosophical outlook, with one comment reading: "The right appointment is the much better option than the quick appointment. Fans moaned on here the other day when it seemed he'd walk out on Rosenborg as he would be "another Matos" to us and leave us quickly. Now they moan he isn't leaving them in the lurch. You have to laugh.".

Whilst uncertainty on the managerial front could be a hindrance for Swansea, especially with games against Bristol City, Bolton Wanderers and Charlton Athletic on the horizon potentially before a decision is made, in the short-term, the presence of Williams and Co. on the touchline may be a major benefit against Cardiff.

With the quartet boasting over 1,200 appearances for the club, they are aware, more than most, of how much this derby means to the locals, especially having lost the last meeting to a Bluebirds side who were ultimately relegated in rock-bottom to League One.

It also remains to be seen whether an upturn in form lands the Wales assistant a chance of the permanent role, but that will not be on Williams' mind right now.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

In a recent development, extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen mentioned: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

In a recent development, villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

According to recent reports, yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

To invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

In a recent development, there were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

Jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

Bellingham's influence attracted widespread praise from the Spanish media, with several publications describing him as the decisive figure in Madrid's transformation.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

His spectacular volley was described as a beautiful and devastating goal, with the newspaper suggesting the Englishman's arrival completely transformed the contest.

Mundo Deportivo labelled Bellingham a "superestrella" - 'superstar' - and suggested that he is right now Madrid's best player, while highlighting how his introduction changed the game.

According to recent reports, elDesmarque were equally enthusiastic, awarding the midfielder 9/10 and naming him their MVP. They highlighted his immediate influence, spectacular goal and assist for Vinicius, describing his 45 minutes as an outstanding exhibition.

Recent findings suggest that real Madrid-focused publications Defensa Central and madridistaReal went even further, awarding him 10/10 and 9.5/10 respectively. Both considered his introduction the turning point in Madrid's victory.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER also marvelled at his volley, with several commentators comparing the technical brilliance of the finish to something Zinedine Zidane might have produced - 'It's like Zizou,' one remarked.

Mourinho was equally impressed, describing the England international's performance as "absolutamente devastador" - 'absolutely devastating'.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

The statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played notable roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

Receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. His goal may have been the highlight, but it was his all-round contribution that made this one of his most impressive performances of the season.

Sources indicate that it's the first meeting between the two sides since the play-off semi-final last season, which Spygate ultimately overshadowed. Ahead of the first leg, Boro officials caught a Saints analyst illegally spying on their training session.

According to recent reports, the games went ahead, and Southampton prevailed in extra time after neither side could be separated in 180 minutes. However, the EFL would then expel Tonda Eckert's side from the play-off final and reinstate Middlesbrough to take on Hull City at Wembley.

Industry observers note that since the Tigers beat Boro in May, the rivalry between both fanbases has been brewing, and was stoked by Eckert being handed just a fine and a suspended sentence by the FA for his role in the operation last month. A week ago, the German was given a upcoming contract at St Mary's.

Fans of clubs can often play down the importance of games, or brand something as "their cup final, not ours," when discussing a matchup between two new rivals, but deep down, both Southampton and Middlesbrough fans want to get one over each other on Friday night.

Peart-Harris, who took his chance back in the starting eleven for the first time in two months on Tuesday night with a goal and an assist in the 2-1 win over Swansea City, watched on from home as Spygate played out back in May, given he wasn't at the club.

However, the 24-year-old knows how much the game means on Friday, and is looking forward to being a part of it.

It has been revealed that "Everyone was watching it [the spygate developments]," he mentioned, per the Northern Echo. "I remember watching the semi-final, and then I think maybe a week later you hear the news about what happened. So now, it's definitely something I’m excited to be a part of.

"Friday's a massive game. It’s a massive football game before anything else, but the rivalry that we now have makes it even better.".

On how the rest of the team feels heading into the game, a lot of them will be looking to pick up a substantial win to almost right the wrongs of the last time they were down at St Mary's in the play-off semi-finals.

Industry observers note that "The boys are looking forward to Friday. Hopefully we go down there, and we play our football, we stick to what we know and get a result," he continued.

Industry observers note that "We're ready, and we’re excited. I think we're just more excited about the game of football that's going to actually happen, because we know they like to play football, we like to play football, so I think tactically it's going to be a great game for everyone to watch.

"Our aim will be to go down and just get a win.".

As Peart-Harris said, first and foremost, though, Friday night will be a great chance for two of the best sides in the division to go head-to-head.

Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert are widely regarded as two of the brightest up-and-coming coaches in the game, and in the past year since they both took over at their respective clubs, the brand of football being played has been fascinating to watch.

This season, Boro have picked up 35 points, while Southampton have collected 32, albeit the four-point deduction handed to them in the wake of the Spygate charges by the EFL means that they sit on 28, seven points adrift of their visitors on Friday.

According to recent reports, who do you think comes out on top on Friday? Let us know in the comments.

It has been revealed that the Teessiders have a tough task on their hands, with Eckert's side utterly dominant at home this season. The only side to have come away with any points from St Mary's through eight games were Bolton Wanderers, who needed to rely on a good defensive display to grind out a 0-0 draw.

It'll be intriguing to see if Boro set up any differently to help combat an unstoppable force on their home patch. Either way, these two teams, and both managers, are destined for the Premier League, and it'll be fun to see them lock horns for the first time this season.

Ultimately, this brooding rivalry is more to do with those in the stands, and perhaps the two coaches in the dugouts, too, even if both have since buried the hatchet after the incident back in May.

The Southampton players who were there to play out the semi-final in the play-offs last season likely weren't to know what Eckert and co were doing to help prepare them for games, and aren't really to blame. Taylor Harwood-Bellis, who was the pantomime villain, mocking Aidan Morris with a spy celebration after Shea Charles' winner, is no longer at the club.

They will be emotionally charged by the atmosphere inside St Mary's on Friday, though, which will have a little more of an edge to it. As mentioned earlier, both sets of fans may pretend not to care, but they do, deep down.

A red-hot atmosphere and two good footballing sides should create a wonderful cocktail of Championship football, and if both teams are up for it, it could go down as one of the games of the season already.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.
  • It has been revealed that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads.
  • According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a fresh wave of signings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.

It has been revealed that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a fresh wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

It has been revealed that at present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

Sources indicate that should the newly introduced rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

Industry observers note that in January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

It is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund announced a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

It has been revealed that because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

According to recent reports, the Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

According to recent reports, strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Recent findings suggest that five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He states the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater mentioned.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day aims back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Industry observers note that drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Industry observers note that squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar matter. Players who fall outside a manager’s prepares rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s intends after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

Mauricio Pochettino praised Manchester United’s character and spirit after his side earned a 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United travelled to Portugal looking to respond after their disappointing 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge. They indicated a much-improved performance away from home, although a number of costly moments prevented the new head coach from celebrating his first victory.

Bruno Fernandes scored twice on his return to the stadium, putting United ahead after Luis Suarez had given Sporting the lead. The home striker also scored twice, including a penalty, to ensure the points were shared.

Senne Lammens had earlier saved a Suarez spot-kick, but the United goalkeeper was involved in another penalty incident that allowed the Sporting forward to find the net. United also had two goals ruled out, while Youri Tielemans was sent off late in the contest.

Despite the frustrating outcome, Pochettino was pleased with what he saw from his players.

The Argentine felt United controlled large periods of the first half but were disappointed to go into the break behind.

Sources indicate that “The first half I think we controlled the game, I think we dominated. We were disappointed to finish the first half 1-0 down,” Pochettino said after the game.

It has been revealed that “The second half I think we started the way we want to play. That is the style, the character. That is the way we want to establish and feeling this way we can perform.”.

The United boss also made it clear that he was proud of the players despite the decisions and incidents that went against them.

“I’m so proud of my players. I think it was a very tough game. I liked the team during 90 minutes, in the way that we showed personality and character.”.

Pochettino felt his side had been punished repeatedly in key moments.

Sources indicate that “In the second half, we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half. We were aggressive and I think that is the way we want to play,” he added.

After the heavy defeat at Anfield, United showed a different level of fight in Lisbon. The draw will still feel like a missed opportunity for Manchester United and Pochettino. However, the Argentine manager believes his players are beginning to embrace the style of play he wants.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeff Stelling had backed QPR for relegation from the Championship, as they now chase promotion to the Premier League.

It has been a positive campaign so far for the R’s, who are in the play-off places, and they have played some good football under Julien Stephan.

This has come on the back of an inconsistent first season under the Frenchman, which ultimately saw QPR finish 15th.

Therefore, it was hard to predict exactly how QPR would perform this season. Whilst there had been some encouraging signs under Stephan, the Londoners lost eight of their last 13 games in the previous season, which included four straight defeats at the end.

So, there was frustration among the supporters that they couldn’t build on a decent start, and many wondered whether they would take that negative momentum into the 2026/27 season.

And, it clearly influenced Stelling, with the TalkSPORT presenter and former Soccer Saturday host predicting relegation for QPR back in August.

It should be said that Stelling made it clear he had no problem with the R’s, and he even admitted he would ‘offend’ their fans, and that he ‘hopes’ he would be wrong.

Pleasingly for QPR, it looks like he will be, as Stephan’s side are 16 points clear of the bottom three, and they’re just seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough, so they are certainly focusing on the other end of the table right now.

We all make calls that are way off, and that looks to be the case with Stelling and QPR here.

The Championship is notoriously difficult, and that unpredictability is why it’s such an enthralling league, even if it was a bold shout to say the R’s could be relegated.

Nevertheless, they are having a good season so far, and most fans would’ve snapped your hand off to be in the play-offs right now, particularly with the way the team are playing.

That’s probably the most encouraging aspect of everything for the R’s, as it doesn’t feel like they’re in a false position, and, if anything, they maybe deserve to be higher in the table.

All credit for that goes to Stephan, as he has built a stylish, attacking side that has proven they can compete with the best teams in this league.

So, the focus for QPR will be to make Stelling’s prediction look even worse come May, when they will hope to be back in the Premier League.

That may seem like a long shot when you consider the resources of the clubs they are competing against, but, as outlined above, they are a very good Championship team right now.

In a recent development, will QPR win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

There will be concerns about how sustainable a promotion push is, and the lack of depth in certain areas, such as the final third, could be their undoing.

Therefore, January will be crucial, and the R’s may need reinforcements if they are to make this season a truly memorable one.

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Recent findings suggest that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

It has been revealed that carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

According to recent reports, it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Industry observers note that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It has been revealed that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

It has been revealed that spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

It has been revealed that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

In a recent development, 3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

Sources indicate that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

Sources indicate that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

Sources indicate that the strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

According to recent reports, the spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after significant-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that it is understood that he is undergoing specialist knee treatment in an attempt to expedite his recovery, although reports in Brazil suggest that he could be out for up to four weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend with a growing treatment table and a lot of questions for Xabi Alonso to answer before Saturday’s visit of Bournemouth.

Sources indicate that the main concern revolves around Joao Pedro. Chelsea’s current player of the season rescued a point against newly promoted Hull, but he suffered a knock and sat out the damaging 3-0 defeat at Brentford. The problem also prompted his removal from Brazil’s squad shortly after he had returned to it.

Sources indicate that it is understood that he is undergoing specialist knee treatment in an attempt to expedite his recovery, although reports in Brazil suggest that he could be out for up to four weeks. No date has yet been set, but a return later in October looks most likely.

It has been revealed that there is more good news elsewhere. Cole Palmer was among the players called up to the latest England squad, which did not go down too well with Thomas Tuchel.

According to recent reports, the midfielder has been recovering from a persistent groin injury and has been working with a rehab coach. He is likely to be fit this weekend.

Sources indicate that moises Caicedo has also struggled with an injury this season, playing just 14 minutes across the campaign. He’s spent the majority of time on the bench recovering from a bad calf injury, which ruled him out for most of the season.

He made his only appearance as a substitute against his former club Brighton, but the game was red-flagged for Ecuador’s friendlies, so he did not play.

Alonso said before the Brentford match that the player would be ready to return. It seems to be the case, unless something went wrong.

It has been revealed that captain Reece James missed the Brentford game with yet another hamstring problem. Alonso said he only just missed out, so a return seems likely.

It has been revealed that there may also be debuts. Marco Palestra, the £27m signing from Atalanta, has been sidelined since a training injury just before the opening match against Fulham. He is back in full training and was expected to feature in a behind-closed-doors friendly with Portsmouth. Chelsea lost 2-0. Emmanuel Emegha, injured after scoring against Bromley in July, is also pushing for involvement.

Less clear is the position of Jamie Gittens. He limped off with an ankle injury playing for England Under-21s against Kazakhstan and was seen on crutches. Mike Penders is fine after a quad scare on Belgium duty. Returning to the bench against Turkey.

Chelsea badly need a lift. Defeat at Brentford before the break left Alonso’s side looking shaky, and a squad stretched by injuries has not helped.

Sources indicate that saturday brings a chance to steady things. If Palmer, James and Caicedo are available, with Palestra and Emegha potentially adding fresh options, the picture will look much brighter at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro’s absence will still sting. However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

It has been revealed that an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026.

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues presently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

In a recent development, milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:29.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.

The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.

Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

However, subsequent scans proved positive, with the Spanish goalkeeper avoiding a serious injury and not requiring surgery.

There have been suggestions that Raya could only be sidelined for a matter of days and might therefore be in contention to face City, but Arteta was unwilling to offer any guarantees after the Dortmund draw.

Sources indicate that "No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately," the Arsenal manager noted (via the Evening Standard). "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].".

Arsenal will therefore have to wait for further clarity on their first-choice goalkeeper, with Kepa potentially required to retain his place against Enzo Maresca's side, who also drew at home to Napoli this midweek.

Kepa produced a reasonably solid display in Germany, with Arteta describing his performance as "really good" and insisting that Arsenal fully trust their goalkeepers.

The Spaniard made three saves and received a 7.5 Sofascore rating, making him the Gunners' third-best performer on the night. His expected goals prevented figure of 0.38 also reflected a positive contribution.

According to recent reports, there were, however, a few moments that offered cause for concern. Kepa was wrong-footed for Dortmund's goal, while he parried a disallowed effort back into a dangerous area and did not look as assured as Raya when dealing with crosses.

Arteta is nevertheless confident in his deputy, saying: "We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.".

It is encouraging that Kepa has Arteta's backing, but there would understandably be some apprehension about him starting against a side of City's calibre. Raya's command of his penalty area and reliability have made him an important figure for Arsenal, and his absence would be a significant setback.

However, if the first-choice goalkeeper is not ready, Kepa will have to step up when called upon.
